demographics.trauma_type: Unexpected or traumatic death of a loved one

Maladaptive Strategies.value: I avoid eating or restrict food as a way of coping

Memory.value: When I have memories of what happened I sometimes hear things in my head that I heard during the frightening event.
When the memory returns I feel so overwhelmed by emotion that I have to stop
I remember the frightening event as a few moments, and each moment is a picture in my mind.

Negative Appraisals.value: I have lost my faith in people, life, or a higher power
Nothing in my life feels meaningful anymore
My life has been destroyed by the trauma

issues.explanation: For trauma type 'unexpected or traumatic death of a loved one', the body-focused appraisals 'I can no longer trust my own body' and 'I feel ashamed of what happened to my body' are hard to reconcile clinically unless the patient also directly experienced major bodily violation/injury, which is not reflected elsewhere in the profile.

The memory items imply vivid sensory reliving of the traumatic event ('hear things ... heard during the frightening event') and fragmented visual snapshots, which can occur in PTSD, but here they are not well matched to the selected appraisals: the profile centers on bodily shame/unreliability rather than grief/death-related meanings of the event.

'Avoid Work or Study: Going to work or study' is not impossible, but in this profile it appears weakly integrated: there are no trigger or threat items tying work contexts to the trauma, and the formulation does not include trigger/threat pathways. The coping profile otherwise concerns sleep delay and undereating, so work avoidance feels insufficiently anchored.

issues.item: Body Shame: I feel ashamed of what happened to my body
issues.explanation: For trauma involving the unexpected or traumatic death of a loved one, body-focused shame is clinically hard to reconcile unless there was also direct bodily violation, injury, or assault. The rest of the profile centers grief-related loss, meaning, and intrusive memory phenomena, so this item appears inconsistent with the trauma type and with the other selected items.

vignette: Samantha, a 46-year-old forensic analyst of Oceania descent, has been struggling since the unexpected death of her husband in a car accident six months ago. The traumatic event continues to dominate her thoughts and behaviors, significantly impacting her daily life and sense of self. On that fateful day, Samantha was at work when she received the call that changed everything. She vividly recalls hearing her colleague's voice trembling as they conveyed the news over the phone. Since then, any auditory cues reminiscent of that moment trigger intense distress. The sound of a phone ringing now sends waves of anxiety through her body, often forcing her to avoid answering calls altogether. Samantha has come to believe that her life was irrevocably altered by this event. She feels that nothing in her world holds meaning anymore and has lost faith in the stability and goodness of others and even the idea of a higher power guiding her life. These negative appraisals have led her to adopt several maladaptive coping mechanisms. One of these is avoiding work, which she now sees as an endless cycle of reminders and triggers. To escape this reality, Samantha often stays up until very late, struggling with insomnia and undereating, feeling that food no longer offers any comfort. Her memories of the accident are fragmented snapshots that replay in her mind at unexpected times. She hears snippets of the phone conversation and the sounds from the day leading up to the call, each memory overwhelming her with a flood of emotions so intense that she is forced to pause whatever she is doing. These intrusive thoughts have become unbearable, leading Samantha to further withdraw from social interactions and work responsibilities. Samantha’s sense of life being destroyed by trauma has only intensified over time, creating a self-reinforcing cycle where her maladaptive strategies exacerbate the very symptoms they are meant to alleviate. Her undereating and avoidance behaviors have led to significant weight loss and a noticeable decline in job performance. Colleagues often notice that she appears distracted and frequently takes breaks during work hours. The fear of reliving those moments through memory flashbacks has pushed Samantha into deeper isolation, further eroding her belief in the possibility of finding meaning or stability in life again. This cycle is perpetuated by her maladaptive behaviors: the avoidance of work due to overwhelming memories leads to more undereating and sleep deprivation, which in turn intensifies the frequency and intensity of intrusive thoughts. What finally brought Samantha to seek help was a particularly disturbing flashback that occurred during an important work meeting, causing her significant distress and embarrassment. She is most afraid of being overwhelmed by these memories again but also hopes for some sense of stability and meaning in her life. Through therapy, she aims to address the deep-seated negative beliefs that have taken root since her husband's death, hoping to break this cycle and find a way forward. Samantha’s current state leaves her feeling trapped in a relentless loop of distressing memories and maladaptive coping mechanisms, but there is a glimmer of hope as she begins to explore avenues for healing and regaining control over her life.
